title: A closed terrarium recycles its own moisture and may need water only a few times a year
alt: Green leafy cuttings and a spider plant growing in dark soil behind glass, with a small stone ornament among them.

posts.facebook:
Picture a small garden under glass that needs watering only a few times a year.

A closed terrarium is a sealed glass jar of plants. It recycles its own moisture, so the RHS (the Royal Horticultural Society, the UK's gardening charity) says it usually needs only a few small waterings a year. Ferns, mosses and small tropical plants suit a closed jar. Succulents and cacti suit an open bowl.

Workshops at botanic gardens and garden centers show you how to layer the gravel, compost and moss, and you take your terrarium home. At RHS Garden Bridgewater in Salford, England, you bring your own clear glass container.

Closed jar or open bowl: which would you make?

How to start, and where to go → https://dontdieretired.com/list/make-a-terrarium/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=things-to-do
